solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Universal policy cleared for adoption of case covering

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the case is taken inside the emptied word
a word cleared of its contents keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: a holster is a case for a pistol

explanation.surface: An insurance policy that has been approved for taking out cover on a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case covering' reads as one phrase, but 'case' is the holster and 'covering' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholstery is the padded fabric layer that covers sofas and chairs.

clue.text: Excess of European intervention finally in protein

parts.note: a glut is an excess or oversupply

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Too much European meddling ends up in the protein, a complaint about food regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the protein found in wheat and other cereals.

clue.text: Update tif?

parts.note: the clue word is the word fit written backwards, that is, fit given in retro fashion

explanation.surface: A terse query about updating a TIF image file.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: put FIT in retro, going backwards, and you get the clue's 'tif'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrofit is to modernise something by adding newer parts, a kind of update.

clue.text: Cakes sent up and put down

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: buns are small cakes

explanation.surface: Cakes are mocked and disparaged, as if a bakery were ridiculed.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to rebuff or slight them, to put them down.

clue.text: Agreement reached when girl is working instead of starting to tire

indicators.note: instead of says one piece takes another's place in the name

parts.note: Constance is a girl's name

indicators.note: starting to points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: on means working, as a machine switched on

explanation.surface: A deal is struck once a girl gets back to work rather than growing weary.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of 'tire' in CONSTANCE is replaced by ON, giving CONS-ON-ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonance means harmony or accord, a state of agreement.

clue.text: Almost hit on shortened playing field being returned for sport

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short of its last letter

parts.note: to sock someone is to hit them

indicators.note: returned means the piece is read backwards

parts.note: rec is a short form of recreation ground, a public playing field

explanation.surface: A ball nearly struck onto a smaller pitch and sent back, in some sport.
explanation.walkthrough: A rec is a British local recreation ground, a public park used for games.
explanation.definitionFit: Soccer is the name for association football, a team sport.

clue.text: Central England N

parts.note: the letter N is the middle one of the word lands, so the clue's N is what the answer read as an instruction yields

explanation.surface: Looks like a map label: central England, north.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'middle of LANDS', which is N. N also looks like north, which misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midlands is the name for the central region of England, around Birmingham.

clue.text: Remain with guy for support

definitions.meaning: a rope or wire that braces a mast, like a guy rope
a ... is also a prop or support, as in corset ...

explanation.surface: Stick around with a man who will back you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: remaining in place, a bracing rope, and a prop.

clue.text: One studies certain relics so potential goal needs reassessing

indicators.note: reassessing suggests the letters are looked at afresh and put in a new order

explanation.surface: A scientist reassesses a promising aim when relics turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: A palaeontologist is a scientist who studies fossils, the relics of ancient life.

clue.text: Stagger bare-headed to animal

indicators.note: bare-headed means the word loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: to totter is to stagger unsteadily

explanation.surface: Someone without a hat staggers towards an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a river-dwelling mammal, one example of an animal.

clue.text: At heart, a simple friend

parts.note: basic means simple or plain
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Deep down, a straightforward friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Basically and at heart both mean fundamentally, in essence.

clue.text: Close relative of Big Bertha? He's a rogue!

definitions.meaning: Big Bertha was a huge German howitzer of the First World War, so its offspring would be the child of a firearm
a scamp or rascal, used affectionately

explanation.surface: A family tie to a famous wartime cannon, and an exclamation about a rascal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old affectionate term for a rascal, and literally names a gun's offspring.

clue.text: Little man has vivid account of lands and peoples

parts.note: Geo is a short form of the man's name George
graphic describes an account that is vivid and detailed

explanation.surface: A small fellow gives a colourful description of countries and their inhabitants.
explanation.definitionFit: Geography studies the earth's regions and populations, so the adjective relates to them.

clue.text: Transform Parisian and his wife

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name, standing for a Parisian
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogy tables

explanation.surface: A Parisian and his spouse undergo a makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to restore or refresh it, making it over anew.

clue.text: A sick crew start spouting rubbish jokes!

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb or adjective suggests a mess, so these letters are jumbled
start points to the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An unwell crew begins talking nonsense and cracking jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The S from 'start spouting' joins A SICK CREW, and 'rubbish' shuffles all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisecracks are witty or flippant remarks, quips and jokes.

clue.text: Quantative chemical breakdown needs preparing a lot, necessarily

indicators.note: preparing suggests making the letters ready by putting them into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Lab analysis requires a lot of preparation, as any chemist would say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quantative' is the setter's spelling of quantitative.
explanation.definitionFit: Electroanalysis measures the amount of a substance using electrical methods in chemistry.

clue.text: Clergyman leaves type of 20, making way for a measure of paint

indicators.note: leaves says the clergyman departs from the longer word
making way for says another piece takes the vacated place

parts.note: 20 is HORROR, and revulsion is a kind of horror or disgust
Rev is short for reverend, a clergyman
an em is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A vicar steps aside from a fright to make room for a paint measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: REV goes out of REVULSION and EM takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is a water-based paint, commonly used on interior walls.

clue.text: Inefficient person lacked, um, organisation

indicators.note: organisation suggests the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A hesitant remark that someone was short of organisational skills.
explanation.definitionFit: A lame duck is someone or something ineffective and in need of help.

clue.text: Teenager that half FT readers go before

indicators.note: go before places the readers ahead of the other piece

parts.note: the readers of the Financial Times are you, addressed by the setter

indicators.note: half means the first two of the four letters of that

explanation.surface: A teenager whom some Financial Times readers precede.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, typically an adolescent or teen.

clue.text: Fear time is short to obtain glasses to accommodate bishop

indicators.note: to obtain means to take in, so the shortened time holds the rest

parts.note: hr is the short form of hour, a time

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so the glasses hold the bishop

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacle lenses
RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Anxiety as time runs out to get spectacles for a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasses as OO is a visual convention: two round lenses. A bishop is addressed as the Right Reverend.
explanation.definitionFit: Horror is intense fear or dread.

clue.text: Said area has a spasm of muscular pain

indicators.note: said indicates the word is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a room is an area or space
a tic is a muscular spasm or twitch

explanation.surface: An area is said to have a muscle spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatic describes conditions causing pain and stiffness in muscles and joints.

clue.text: Time to admit being fat

parts.note: to allow is to admit or concede

explanation.surface: It is time to own up to being overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallow is hard animal fat, used for candles and soap.

clue.text: Chatter about temper tantrum at university eatery

indicators.note: about means the chatter goes around the other pieces

parts.note: gab is idle chatter
a strop is a fit of bad temper, in British slang

explanation.surface: Gossip about a student's tantrum in a campus restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: A strop is British slang for a sulk or tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub that serves good-quality food, a kind of eating place.

clue.text: Double-crossing scoundrels not found around here?

definitions.text: Double-crossing scoundrels not found around here?

parts.words: Double-crossing scoundrels not found around here?
parts.note: double-crossing scoundrels are deserters, and the joke is that deserters would hardly be absent from a desert

explanation.surface: A wry question about where traitors are absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Deserters, playing on desert, are absent here: a desert, ironically, empty of deserters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast desert in Mongolia and northern China, a place one might expect such deserters.

clue.text: Round pound

definitions.meaning: a police officer's ... is the regular round they patrol
to pound is to strike repeatedly

explanation.definitionFit: One word means both a patrol route and to strike repeatedly.

clue.text: In the beginning, did Egyptians learn that Alexandria was built on it?

definitions.text: In the beginning, did Egyptians learn that Alexandria was built on it?

indicators.note: in the beginning points to the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A history question about where Alexandria was founded.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandria stands on the Nile's fan-shaped river mouth in northern Egypt.

clue.text: It is supposed to keep watch on one's progression in life

definitions.text: It is supposed to keep watch on one's progression in life

parts.words: It is supposed to keep watch on one's progression in life
parts.note: keep watch suggests a timepiece, here the body's internal timer tracking ageing

explanation.surface: A description of something monitoring how one's life advances.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the body's supposed inner timer governing rhythms and fertility over the years.
